findings.title: Wrong lightness swapped on .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: The rule `.topic-meta-data h5 a` originally set color to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, swapping the lightness values. In the light theme the color now becomes `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` (a much lighter gray than the original 30%) and the dark theme becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` instead of the intended `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`. The correct fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: the appearance of every embedded-post meta header link changes (light theme) and the dark theme gets the wrong contrast.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on .topic-map h3
findings.body: The rule `.topic-map h3` originally set color to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, losing the original 20% lightness on the primary side. The intended mirror is 20% ↔ 80%, so it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. Consequence: mobile topic-map headings now render in mid-gray instead of the previous very-dark gray in the light theme, and mid-gray in the dark theme rather than near-white. Other selectors in the same `.topic-map` block (h4, span.domain, .number/i) were updated correctly with 50/50, 50/50 and 20/80, so this one stands out.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on .custom-message-length
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping the two lightness values. The intended mirror is 70% ↔ 30%, so the correct call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Consequence: in light themes the flag-modal character-counter text is now a darker gray (30%) instead of the previous light gray (70%); the dark-theme branch is wrong too. The desktop counterpart `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` line 94 has the same selector and was correctly updated to 70/30, so this is a clear inconsistency between desktop and mobile.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on .group-member-info .name
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, dropping the 30% lightness. The intended mirror is 30% ↔ 70%, so the correct call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: member-name text inside user-stream group-member-info is rendered in mid-gray on light themes instead of the original darker gray, and the dark-theme contrast is wrong. `.group-member-info .title` immediately below (also changed to 50/50) was correctly mirrored from its own original 50% lightness, so the two siblings end up with different colors in both themes despite originating from different lightnesses.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Mirror of the desktop/user.scss issue. `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The intended fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: mobile group-member-info name text loses its darker emphasis versus the sibling `.title` rule (which legitimately stays 50/50) and the dark-theme color is wrong.
